name: Thornwork — Horn and Antler Geneware Culture
description: Thornwork is the dedicated community built around cosmetic horn, antler, and cranial ridge geneware — modifications that range from small decorative nubs to elaborate branching antler structures requiring structural reinforcement of the skull. Unlike broader geneware communities, Thornwork has developed its own dense aesthetic language: the shape, size, and adornment of horns signal status, identity, and affiliation within the community. Horns are never hidden — concealment is considered shameful. Members 'dress' their horns with hand-wrapped cord, metalwork, small offerings, and seasonal adornments in a practice called 'crowning.' The community's spiritual dimension emerged organically, centered on the concept of growth as identity.
cultural_impact: Thornwork has forced practical urban design responses — several transit systems have widened certain clearances after Thornwork members organized accessibility complaints. Their crowning aesthetic has been heavily copied in Tier 4-5 fashion without community credit, a source of ongoing tension.
locations: The Crown Room (community space, Tier 2 North)
Thornwork Annual Gathering, Humboldt Park Remnant
story_hooks: A Thornwork member's geneware begins growing beyond predicted parameters — the unlicensed geneware clinic that did the work has closed, and corporate clinics won't touch unlicensed modifications without a full reset.
A Tier 4 fashion house releases a 'Thornwork-inspired' line with a synthetic horn accessory — Thornwork members must decide between legal action, public protest, or ignoring it.
A death in the community leaves behind a set of extraordinarily rare crowned antlers — Thornwork tradition says they should be interred with the body, but the family wants to sell them.
